title: It is time to make prior authorization reform a reality — AMA report on the 2024 Prior Authorization Physician Survey

history.reason: Read and summarized during the first discovery session (issue #7)

source_type: industry association article reporting its own physician survey (n=1,000, late 2024)
reliability: Primary publisher of the underlying survey. The AMA advocates for prior-authorization reform, so framing is advocacy-aligned; the survey figures are the association's own reported results.
findings: Practices completed an average of 39 prior authorization requests per physician per week.
Handling those requests takes an average of 13 hours of physician and staff time per physician per week.
82% of surveyed physicians reported patients abandoned treatment due to prior authorization issues; 94% said poorer clinical outcomes were linked to prior authorization.
More than one in four physicians said prior authorization had triggered a serious adverse event (hospitalization, permanent impairment, or death) for a patient in their care.
75% of surveyed physicians reported denials had risen over the past five years.
limitations: Physician self-report; no independent time-motion verification.
The article does not break results down by practice size, so the burden on small independent practices specifically is not measured here.
Published by an organization campaigning on this issue.
